Definition: plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernæ:--taverns.
BiblicalUsage: The Three Taverns was a roadside stop on the Appian Way, about thirty-three miles from Rome, where brethren came out to meet Paul. The word is Latin in Greek dress: taverns, or huts and wooden buildings, a staging post for travellers. When Paul saw the believers waiting there, Luke says he thanked God and took courage.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the welcome at the Three Taverns matters because Paul had waited so long to reach Rome. I hold that God often sends courage through ordinary believers standing on an ordinary road.
